system.name: MetaSapiens
system.one_liner: a point-based neural rendering system that delivers real-time, human-quality rendering on mobile devices via efficiency-aware pruning and foveated rendering

content.subject: how a scene's 3D Gaussian ellipsoids are projected onto an image-plane tile as ellipses, sorted by depth, and combined to shade one pixel

elements.name: A
elements.role: one 3D Gaussian ellipsoid representing a scene point

elements.name: B
elements.role: second ellipsoid; its projection lies outside the highlighted pixel tile

elements.name: C
elements.role: third ellipsoid, closest to the image plane so integrated first when shading the pixel

elements.name: Image plane
elements.role: the 2D surface all scene ellipsoids are projected (splatted) onto

elements.name: 2x2 tile
elements.role: one pixel tile on the image plane used to group intersecting ellipses for shading

elements.name: a
elements.role: projected ellipse of ellipsoid A on the image plane

elements.name: b
elements.role: projected ellipse of ellipsoid B, drawn outside the highlighted tile

elements.name: c
elements.role: projected ellipse of ellipsoid C, closest ellipse to the image plane

elements.name: Pixel p
elements.role: the specific pixel whose colour is computed from the intersecting ellipses a, c, d, e

elements.name: camera
elements.role: viewpoint the scene is rendered from

relations.what: ellipsoid A is projected/splatted to ellipse a on the image plane
ellipsoid B is projected to ellipse b
ellipsoid C is projected to ellipse c
ellipsoid D is projected to ellipse d
ellipsoid E is projected to ellipse e
the intersecting ellipses (a, c, d, e) are blended front-to-back to shade pixel p

content.key_idea: The general point-based neural rendering pipeline reduces to three per-tile steps: project each scene ellipsoid to an image-plane ellipse, sort the intersecting ellipses by depth, and blend their colours front-to-back to shade the pixel.
content.reading_order: left to right: the cluster of labelled 3D Gaussian ellipsoids (A-E) in the shaded scene region, projected diagonally onto the Image plane, zooming into the 2x2 tile where ellipses a, c, d, e overlap at Pixel p, with the camera icon at bottom right marking the viewpoint

palette.used_for: grey radial-gradient background circle marking the 3D scene region

style.stroke: medium (~0.57pt) dashed grey strokes for each ellipsoid's axis line; thin black lines for the image-plane grid
style.arrows: thin plain lines projecting from each ellipsoid through the image plane toward the camera, without arrowheads
style.icons: about a dozen raster (bitmap) images render the soft-edged translucent ellipsoid blobs (roughly 59% of the figure area); a small vector camera glyph at bottom right

encoding.line_style_means: dashed lines mark each ellipsoid's principal axis; thin solid lines are projection rays from ellipsoid centres through the image plane to the camera
encoding.state_means: not applicable; a single static frame with no before/after state
encoding.marker_means: no numbered markers; matching upper/lower-case letters (A to a, ..., E to e) are the only correspondence markers
encoding.emphasis: zooming into the 2x2 tile isolates exactly the ellipses relevant to Pixel p, and an arrow into 'Pixel p' focuses attention on the one pixel the accompanying volume-rendering equation computes
reusable_patterns: matching upper-case 3D objects to lower-case 2D projections via colour and a projection line, with a magnified tile inset showing pixel-level detail

ellipse b sits close to the highlighted 2x2 tile, which could be misread as intersecting it like a, c, d, e do

N is the number of ellipses intersecting p (i.e., a, c, d, e in Fig. 1)

summary: This figure illustrates the general point-based neural rendering (PBNR) pipeline that MetaSapiens builds on, using 3D Gaussian Splatting as the running example. A scene is parameterized by discrete points, each carrying a 3D Gaussian distribution that gives rise to an ellipsoid (labelled A-E); five such ellipsoids are drawn clustered in a shaded circular scene region. Each ellipsoid is projected ('splatted') through a camera onto a 2D image plane, producing a matching lower-case ellipse (a-e). The figure zooms into one 2x2 pixel tile on the image plane, where ellipses a, c, d and e overlap and intersect a specific Pixel p (b lies just outside this tile); c, being closest to the camera, is integrated first. This illustrates the three-step online rendering pipeline the paper generalizes across all PBNR methods: projection, depth sorting, and rasterization, where a pixel's final colour blends the contributions of every intersecting ellipse from near to far.
summary_zh: 该图展示MetaSapiens所依赖的点基神经渲染(PBNR)通用流程：场景中的高斯点A-E对应椭球，经相机投影到成像平面得到椭圆a-e；放大的2x2像素块内a、c、d、e与像素p相交（b不在块内），按深度排序后混合得到该像素颜色，体现投影、排序、光栅化三步骤。
notes: style.palette reflects only the flat vector fill (#cccccc grey background circle) found in the source-SVG histogram; the vivid A-E/a-e ellipsoid colours are rendered as roughly a dozen embedded raster images (about 59% of the figure area per the measured attributes), not flat vector fills, so their hex values do not appear in the histogram.
